Theme 100 · Camera & edit grammar

Rack Focus

A shallow-depth-of-field film where the focus pull is the storyteller. The hook is sharp on one tab out of 38, the drop racks through blurred dashboards to the Acme Pulse screen, the proof keeps just the anomaly sharp while 13 other metrics melt into bokeh, and the CTA stops down so everything is crisp at last. A focus-puller’s distance scale with taped marks A, B, C sits under every frame.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Focal planes — foreground, subject and background layers with different blur radii
  • Bokeh field — soft circles in teal, coral and amber that turn out-of-focus UI into atmosphere
  • Focus peaking — coral outline glow on whatever is sharp, a real camera-monitor aid
  • Focus scale — dark distance ruler (0.3 m → ∞) with a coral focus dot
  • Tape marks A / B / C — amber focus-puller marks and a rack arrow between them
  • Anomaly card — the only sharp object in the proof beat

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Rack — blur radii swap between layers over 0.6 s (sine.inOut, just over one beat at 120 BPM), starting half a beat early so the new plane is sharp on the downbeat
  • Focus breathing — the sharp layer scales 1.00 → 1.02 during the rack, like a real lens breathing, then settles
  • Stop-down — all blur radii go to 0 and bokeh shrinks to 40% over 1 bar (2 s, power2.out) for the CTA

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Rack focus is the most gentle way to say “look here”: it doesn’t cut or move, it simply chooses. That matches a product whose job is to pick the one metric that matters out of many. It also makes plain UI look cinematic. Risk: any text left in a blurred plane is lost, so keep all copy on the sharp plane or on a flat graphic layer.

Adapt to your product: Layer your product’s screens at different depths: the noise your users face today in front, your product behind, and the one object your product surfaces as the final sharp plane. Every rack should land on something the viewer must read.

References: https://www.studiobinder.com/blog/rack-focus-shot-camera-movement-angles/ (rack focus: shifting the focal plane during a shot) · https://nofilmschool.com/rack-focus (practical uses of rack focus and focus marks)
